list: The official 55-trophy PlayStation 5 list, frozen 2026-11-18: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase and PSNProfiles agree on all 55).
note: CONFIRMED means the requirement is stated in the official trophy description itself. EXPECTED means the method is extrapolated from the official description plus GTA V / GTA Online series patterns and what Rockstar has shown in the GTA VI trailers; it has not been checked in the game yet. GTA VI released 19 Nov 2026 and its trophy list was published before launch, so every method below is a plan, not a verified walkthrough.

sources.exophase: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official names, descriptions, grades): https://www.exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/
sources.official: Rockstar Games — GTA VI official site: https://www.rockstargames.com/VI
sources.psnprofiles: PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophies (grades and PSN progress targets): https://psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi
sources.series: GTA V / GTA Online — series patterns (mission replay, wanted levels, properties, collectibles) used to extrapolate methods
sources.trailer1: Rockstar Games — GTA VI Trailer 1 (Dec 2023): first look at Vice City and Leonida
sources.trailer2: Rockstar Games — GTA VI Trailer 2 (May 2025): Lucia and Jason, Leonida locations, activities shown on screen

trophies.guide: The platinum. It pops automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are yours — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work through the roadmap in order: finish the story first, then the partner and stranger strands, then the collectibles and count-based trophies, and save the long grinds (250 stunts, 100 vehicles, 100 WAiNK locations) for last so they tick over while you play.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Finish all four story chapters and the final mission.
Complete every stranger strand, activity and collectible set the other trophies ask for.
Check the tracker: the platinum unlocks as soon as the counter reads 54 of 54.

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable. 'Gone Fishing' is the opening mission — Lucia and Jason's first job together, shown in the trailers as the pair's return to Vice City. Just play through it: follow the on-screen prompts, drive where the game points you, and the trophy pops at the mission-pass screen. It is the first trophy most players will earn.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
Follow the mission markers and complete each objective.
The trophy unlocks at the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable. Play through every mission in Chapter 1 in order; the chapter ends with a finale mission, and the trophy pops when it is done. If you get stuck on a mission, GTA games let you retry from a checkpoint or skip a failed section after repeated failures — the chapter itself cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Play every Chapter 1 mission in story order.
Finish the chapter finale mission.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter-complete screen appears.

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable. Chapter 2 continues Lucia and Jason's climb through Leonida's underworld — the name is a nod to the drug-money jobs that drive the plot. Clear each mission in order and finish the chapter finale. As with every chapter trophy, mission replay (the series standard since GTA V) means a failed mission never locks you out.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Play every Chapter 2 mission in story order.
Finish the chapter finale mission.
The trophy unlocks at the chapter-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable. Chapter 3 takes the story into the heart of Vice City itself. Work through the missions in order — expect the chapter to introduce new contacts and the bigger heist setups that the later chapters pay off. Finish the finale and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Play every Chapter 3 mission in story order.
Finish the chapter finale mission.
The trophy unlocks at the chapter-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable. Chapter 4 is the last stretch before the finale — the highest-stakes missions of the game, with the biggest payouts and the hardest fights. Clear the missions in order, finish the chapter finale, and this pops right before the final mission trophy.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Play every Chapter 4 mission in story order.
Finish the chapter finale mission.
The trophy unlocks at the chapter-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Gold story trophy, unmissable — but do the partner trophies first. Finish the final mission and this gold pops. Warning: the partner-dependent trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) need your partner beside you in free roam, and some story beats can change who is available afterwards. Clear those two before you start the finale, then enjoy the ending.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Before the finale: earn Hot Together and Retail Therapy while your partner is still freely available.
Play the final mission to its end.
The gold trophy unlocks at the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy, unmissable. 'Breakfast Run' is a named story mission — an early job that sets up the trust between Lucia and Jason (the name says it). Play it when it appears in the mission flow; the trophy pops at the mission-pass screen. If you fail, retry from the checkpoint.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Play the story until the Breakfast Run mission unlocks.
Complete its objectives and reach the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy, unmissable. 'The Cartel Heist' is one of the game's big set-piece heists — expect a planning stage, a crew to assemble, and a loud getaway, following the heist structure GTA V established. Complete the heist and the trophy pops at the pass screen.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Play the story until The Cartel Heist unlocks and finish any setup missions first.
Complete the heist itself.
The trophy unlocks at the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy, unmissable. 'Child's Play' is a named story mission tied to family — likely a job for one of the pair's relatives or a contact's kid, in the GTA tradition of missions that mix crime with domestic chaos. Play it in the story flow and it pops at the pass screen.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Play the story until the Child's Play mission unlocks.
Complete its objectives and reach the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy, unmissable. 'Headliners' is a named story mission — the stylised DWNFALL title suggests a music-scene job, possibly tied to the in-game artists Rockstar showed in the trailers. Complete the mission in the story flow and the trophy pops at the pass screen.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Play the story until the Headliners mission unlocks.
Complete its objectives and reach the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy, unmissable. 'VCIA Takedown' is a job at Vice City International Airport — the pun in the trophy name gives away the theme: a hijacking. Expect a vehicle-theft set piece on the runways or in the cargo areas. Complete it in the story flow and the trophy pops at the pass screen.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Play the story until the VCIA Takedown mission unlocks.
Complete its objectives and reach the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Story mission trophy, unmissable. 'Operation Savage Glory' sounds like a military-style operation — the 'Snow Storm' name hints at a product (or a snowstorm of trouble) at its centre. It is likely one of the bigger late-game missions. Complete it in the story flow and the trophy pops at the pass screen.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Play the story until the Operation Savage Glory mission unlocks.
Complete its objectives and reach the mission-pass screen.

trophies.guide: Gold trophy and the real endgame: 100% completion. In GTA V that meant story missions, stranger missions, hobbies, collectibles and stunts; here the checklist is built from the trophy list itself — every activity, collectible set and count the other trophies name. Use the in-game stats page to see what is left, and use this guide's roadmap: finish the story, then strands, then collectibles, then the long counts. It is the last gold most players earn, just before the platinum.
trophies.name: A Long Road
steps: Finish the story and every stranger strand.
Complete all collectible sets and activity counts the other trophies list.
Open the in-game 100% checklist (stats menu) and clear the remaining items one by one.

trophies.guide: Silver grind: 250 stunts. A 'stunt' in GTA means a jump, a near-miss, a long airtime or a drift — the game counts them as you play, and PSN tracks the total toward 250. Do not grind this separately at first: drive fast, take jumps and ramps in free roam, and use the stunt jumps scattered around Leonida. Once the story is done, farm the remaining count by repeating a short jump loop in a fast car. It is a patience trophy, not a skill one.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Play normally — jumps, near-misses and drifts all count toward the total.
Check the PSN progress counter to see how many of 250 you have.
After the story, repeat a reliable jump loop in a fast car to finish the remainder.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: A sampler trophy: try all 9 activity types once. The trailers show fishing, golf, bowling, drone racing, shooting ranges, arcade games, meditation spots, hunting and more — the 9 counted types are the game's side activities. Open the activities menu (or visit each venue) and do one of each; the trophy pops when the ninth type registers. Do this early — it also unlocks several other trophies' starting points.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Visit the activities list and note the 9 types.
Do one of each: fishing, a race, the range, an arcade game, bowling, a drone race, meditation, hunting and golf (or the game's equivalents).
The trophy pops when the ninth type is tried.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver skill trophy: gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges (PSN's count). The range is a returning GTA activity — timed target courses with pistols, rifles and more. Gold means beating the top time/score on every course. Tips from the series: use a controller for fine aim, learn each course's target layout before going for gold, and do the easy weapon classes first. Expect this to take a focused session or two.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Find a Shooting Range (Ammu-Nation in the series) and open its challenge list.
Work through the 42 challenges, learning each layout first.
Earn gold on every challenge — the trophy pops on the last gold.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a drone race at all 14 locations. Top Fun is the RC/drone brand from GTA V's drone and RC races, and the trailers show drone racing over Leonida. Each location hosts its own race; win it once and it counts. Learn each track's gates and shortcuts, keep the drone low through gates, and do the shorter tracks first. All 14 wins are needed — check the race menu to see which locations are still missing.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Open the Top Fun drone race menu and list the 14 locations.
Race each location and win it once.
The trophy pops when the 14th location is won.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — land, sea or air, across Leonida. Races unlock as you meet contacts and visit race start points; the count is of distinct races, not total wins, so variety matters. Mix street races, off-road, boat and air races. The easiest path: clear the short street races first, then work through the race menu's remaining events one by one.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Open the race menu and note the un-won races.
Win races one by one, favouring short street circuits first.
The trophy pops on the 20th distinct race win.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — do this when Cal offers it. Cal is a fishing contact (likely met through the fishing activity) who challenges you to a fishing contest: catch more, or bigger, fish than him in the time limit. Fishing was shown in the trailers, with rods, boats and tackle. When the challenge appears, take it immediately — a named NPC challenge may not repeat if you refuse it. Use the best rod and bait you have, and fish the spots the game marks.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Unlock fishing and meet Cal through the activity.
Accept his fishing challenge as soon as it is offered — do not put it off.
Out-fish him in the challenge to pop the trophy.

trophies.guide: Play one arcade game to completion. Arcades are a GTA staple — the trailers show neon arcade cabinets — and 'complete' means finishing a full game, not just starting one. Pick the shortest cabinet you find, learn its rules in one practice run, then play it through to the end screen. Any arcade game counts.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade (look for the neon cabinets in Vice City).
Start any game and play it through to its end screen.
The trophy pops when the game completes.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Side-strand trophy: finish Andy's mission chain. Andy is one of the stranger contacts whose missions unlock across the map — play each of his jobs in order until the final one. Stranger strands in GTA usually unlock by visiting a marker or answering a call, so check the map for Andy's icon after each story chapter. The final mission pops the trophy at its pass screen.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Find Andy's first mission marker on the map and play it.
Return for each follow-up mission as the strand unlocks.
Complete his final mission — the trophy pops at the pass screen.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Side-strand trophy: finish Kenton's mission chain. Kenton is another stranger contact with a multi-mission strand — work through his jobs in order. The name 'This Was No Boat Accident' hints his strand involves boats or a marina, so expect water work. Check the map for his marker after story chapters, and finish his final mission for the trophy.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Find Kenton's first mission marker and play it.
Work through his strand mission by mission.
Complete his final mission — the trophy pops at the pass screen.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Side-strand trophy: finish Billy's mission chain. 'The Lone Rider' points to a biker — Billy is likely tied to Leonida's biker gangs, so expect motorcycle missions and gang runs. Play his strand in order, checking the map for his marker between story chapters, and finish his final mission.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Find Billy's first mission marker and play it.
Work through his strand mission by mission.
Complete his final mission — the trophy pops at the pass screen.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver strand trophy: finish 8 stranger mission strands in full. Strangers are the '?' contacts scattered across Leonida — each strand is a chain of 2–5 missions. Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have their own trophy, and those five count toward the eight; find three more strands (check the map after every story chapter, since new markers appear as the story advances). Finishing a strand's final mission counts it — track your progress in the in-game stats.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Play the strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone (5 of 8).
Find three more stranger strands from map markers after each chapter.
Complete each strand's final mission — the trophy pops on the 8th.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Side-strand trophy: finish Randy's mission chain. 'Supply & Demand' suggests a smuggling or supply-running strand — expect fetch-and-deliver jobs across Leonida. Play his missions in order from his map marker, and finish his final mission for the trophy.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Find Randy's first mission marker and play it.
Work through his strand mission by mission.
Complete his final mission — the trophy pops at the pass screen.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Side-strand trophy: finish Tyrone's mission chain. 'Spin On This!' hints at a DJ or music-scene strand — Tyrone is likely tied to Leonida's club scene, which the trailers show heavily. Play his missions in order from his map marker, and finish his final mission for the trophy.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Find Tyrone's first mission marker and play it.
Work through his strand mission by mission.
Complete his final mission — the trophy pops at the pass screen.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots. Meditation is a new Leonida activity — quiet scenic spots (beaches, hilltops, the Everglades-style wetlands) where you sit and breathe for a short scene. The spots are marked once discovered; use the map and check the PSN progress counter. This pairs well with the exploration trophy — do the far-flung spots while you are mapping Leonida anyway.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Find meditation spots (map markers, scenic viewpoints).
Meditate at each one until the scene completes.
The trophy pops at the 18th spot.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — one hunt, one animal. Bret is a hunting contact who asks you to take down a unique animal (a named, one-of-a-kind beast — the series has done this before with rare animals). Do not shoot it before Bret's mission: the trophy is for hunting it for Bret, so the kill only counts inside his strand. When the hunt starts, track the animal, use a scoped rifle, and aim for a clean kill.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Meet Bret and start his hunting strand.
Wait for the unique-animal hunt — do not kill the animal outside the mission.
Take it down cleanly inside the hunt to pop the trophy.

trophies.guide: Silver collectible trophy: complete 3 card sets. Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida — in shops, on benches, in interiors — and each set is a group of cards (a character, a car, a location). Pick up cards as you explore; the collection menu shows which sets are close to complete. Three finished sets pop the trophy, so focus the sets with the fewest cards left. Cards are not missable — they stay in the world.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Pick up collectible cards while exploring (check interiors and landmarks).
Open the collection menu and find the sets nearest completion.
Finish any 3 sets — the trophy pops on the third.

trophies.guide: Silver grind: use the WAiNK app (Leonida's in-game photo/social app, shown in the trailers) at 100 locations. 'WAiNK It' means opening the app at a spot and sharing a photo or check-in — the game counts distinct locations, so you must travel. Do it while exploring for the exploration trophy: WAiNK at every landmark, beach, town and viewpoint you pass. 100 is a lot, so fold it into every other trip rather than grinding it alone.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: Open the WAiNK app at a location and post/check in.
Repeat at new locations while exploring — the game counts distinct spots.
The trophy pops at the 100th location.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's checklist goals — stunt jumps, race wins, collectibles, combat feats — and they stack up naturally as you chase the other trophies. Open the challenges menu to see which are close, then clear the easy ones (short races, simple stunts) to reach 50. This is a milestone trophy: by the time you are halfway through the other counts, it will be near done.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Open the challenges menu and note the nearly-done ones.
Clear easy challenges (races, stunts, collectibles) first.
The trophy pops on the 50th completed challenge.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — do this while your partner is available in free roam, before the finale. With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level (rob a store, shoot up a street, steal a cop car — enough heat that the game shows four stars), then lose it: break line of sight, hide in alleys or off-road, and stay out of the search cones until the stars clear. Doing it with your partner is the whole point — the game checks both of you escape together.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Bring your partner along in free roam (before the final mission).
Build a 4-star wanted level together.
Break line of sight and hide until the stars clear — both of you.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — do this while your partner is available in free roam, before the finale. With your partner beside you, rob three shops in a row without letting your wanted level drop between them: walk in, aim at the clerk, grab the cash, leave, and drive straight to the next shop while the stars stay up. Plan a route of three close shops in advance, keep a fast car outside each one, and do not stop for anything else. If the stars clear, the chain resets.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Bring your partner and pick three close shops in advance.
Rob the first shop and keep your wanted level up.
Drive straight to shops two and three and rob them too — the trophy pops on the third.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — drive or ride 100 distinct vehicle types. The game counts a vehicle as discovered when you first enter or drive it. Leonida's traffic is varied: cars, bikes, boats, planes, trucks and more. Variety is the trick: steal a different car on every street, try boats at the marina, grab a plane at the airport, and register the rare ones with the Scooter Bros app (that also feeds another trophy). The counter is in the stats menu.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Drive a different vehicle at every chance — variety counts, not repeats.
Try boats, planes and bikes as well as cars.
The trophy pops on the 100th distinct vehicle.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is GTA VI's slow-motion aiming mode (the series' Dead Eye-style focus, shown in the trailers). To take down 5 enemies in one use: find a group of enemies (a gang shootout or a wanted-level firefight), trigger Combat Focus, and land killing shots on five of them before the meter runs out. Use a high-damage weapon, aim for headshots, and pick a fight where enemies cluster. If the meter empties at four, just retry — it is a skill check, not a one-shot.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find a firefight with at least 5 clustered enemies.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down 5 before the meter empties.
The trophy pops on the fifth takedown in that single use.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: An airport stunt: leave Vice City International Airport in an 'unscheduled' way — steal a plane (or helicopter) and take off without following the rules. The simplest read: enter VCIA, grab an aircraft from the runway or hangars, and fly out. Expect police attention, so be quick: land on the runway, sprint to a plane, take off and climb. The trophy pops once you are airborne and clear of the airport.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Enter VCIA and reach the runways or hangars.
Steal a plane or helicopter.
Take off and leave the airport airspace — the trophy pops.

trophies.guide: The Rhino is GTA's tank, and this trophy is about getting into one (and surviving the heat it brings). In the series, tanks appear at the military base or during high wanted levels. The practical path: reach a 5-star wanted level and wait for the military response, or find the base and steal a Rhino from inside. Once you are in the tank and the game registers the moment, the trophy pops. Expect a lot of attention — tanks draw the army.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Reach a high wanted level or enter the military base to find a Rhino tank.
Get inside the Rhino.
The trophy pops once you are driving it under fire.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE in the moment — a clean stealth job. Pick a jewelry store, case it first, and rob it without any alarm or detection: go in quiet, avoid the cameras and guards, and get out before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — but you can retry the store later, so it is not a one-chance trophy. Plan the exit before you go in, and keep a fast car parked close.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Pick a jewelry store and plan a quiet approach and exit.
Rob it without being seen or triggering an alarm.
Leave clean — the trophy pops on a fully undetected robbery.

trophies.guide: Silver heist trophy: rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time. Bank vaults are the bigger robbery targets — expect alarms, timers and police chases. Each vault is a job: get in, crack or blow the vault, grab the cash and escape the wanted level. Five successful escapes pop the trophy. Bring a fast getaway car, plan the route out before you go in, and do them one at a time between other work.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Find a bank vault target and plan the getaway first.
Rob the vault and escape the wanted level.
Repeat for 5 vaults — the trophy pops on the fifth escape.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: A classic GTA job: rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks patrol Leonida's roads — spot one, force it to stop (ram it, block it, or shoot the driver), crack the back open and grab the cash, then lose the wanted level. The name nods to GTA V's 'Blitz Play' armored-truck heist. One successful robbery and escape pops the trophy.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Find an armored truck on the road and force it to stop.
Break into the back and take the cash.
Escape the wanted level — the trophy pops.

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — the whole map. Leonida is the state around Vice City: the city itself, the beaches, the Everglades-style wetlands, small towns and farmland. The game counts an area as explored when you enter it. Drive everywhere: take the highways between towns, boat through the wetlands, fly over the far corners. The map screen shows which areas are still grey. This pairs with the WAiNK and meditation trophies — explore once, collect everything on the way.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Drive, boat and fly through every part of the map.
Watch the map screen — grey areas are unexplored.
The trophy pops when all 52 areas are visited.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation from each of the 9 gangs. Gangs run hidden operations around Leonida — drug labs, stash houses, smuggling depots — and robbing one means hitting the location and taking its goods. Nine gangs, nine hits. The map and street intel point to the operations; do them one gang at a time and keep count in the stats menu. Expect armed resistance at each one.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Locate an illegal operation for each of the 9 gangs.
Rob one operation per gang, taking its goods.
The trophy pops when the 9th gang's operation is robbed.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: A pure vibe trophy: have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Go to Ocean Beach (Vice City's famous beachfront, shown in the trailers), find a beach bar or a spot with a view, and order a cocktail. The game checks the location and the drink — sit, sip, and the trophy pops. Do it any time; it is a nice break between missions.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Go to Ocean Beach in Vice City.
Find a beach bar or viewpoint spot.
Order and enjoy a cocktail with the view — the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: A reference to the classic GTA showroom smash: drive a car into (or out of) a vehicle showroom through the glass. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or drive one at the front window, and smash your way out through the glass. The game checks the destruction and the exit — one good smash does it. Any showroom counts; the fastest is the one nearest a main road.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Find a vehicle showroom and get a car to its front glass.
Smash through the glass and out of the showroom.
The trophy pops on the smash exit.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley. Bowling returns from GTA IV — roll a ball, knock down pins, and the 'follow-through' is the animation after your throw. Find the Kolt & Associates alley (a law-firm front, in the GTA tradition of joke businesses), play a frame or a full game, and the trophy pops. It also counts toward the 'try each activity' trophy.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Play a game of bowling.
The trophy pops when the follow-through registers.

trophies.guide: A partnership moment: do something with your partner that the public loves. The description is deliberately vague — in the trailers, Lucia and Jason's partnership is the game's heart, and this likely pops from a story beat or a shared activity that goes viral in Leonida (a WAiNK post, a stunt, a public moment). Play the story and the partner activities; it will come from a shared moment, not a grind. Status: expected — the trigger is not pinned down by the official description.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: Play the story and partner activities together.
Watch for a shared public moment (a viral post or stunt with your partner).
The trophy pops at that partnership beat.

trophies.guide: PSN tracks a count to 500 for this one: make 500 choices. 'Choices' here means the small decisions the game tracks — dialogue picks, activity choices, purchases, responses to strangers. It is a long cumulative counter that grows as you play everything else, so do not chase it directly: play the story, do the strands, try the activities, and it will climb. Check the PSN progress counter to see where you stand.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Play the game broadly — story, strands, activities, shops.
Make dialogue and activity choices whenever offered.
The trophy pops at the 500th tracked choice.

trophies.guide: Fail once, succeed the second time. This trophy is for retrying something after a failure — the natural read is to fail a mission or activity, then pass it on the immediate retry. In GTA, failing a mission and retrying from the checkpoint is routine, so this will likely pop on its own during a hard mission. If it has not popped by the end of the story, pick a mission, fail it once, and pass it on the retry.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: Fail a mission or activity once.
Retry it immediately and pass it on the second attempt.
The trophy pops on the successful retry.

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — a random event. Leonida is full of odd encounters (the series has done UFOs, ghosts and stranger events since GTA V), and this trophy is for stumbling into one. Keep your eyes open while exploring: unusual lights, odd NPCs, strange scenes in remote places. It cannot be forced, but exploring the whole map for the exploration trophy maximises your chances. When something weird happens, the trophy pops.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: Explore remote and unusual parts of Leonida.
Watch for strange events, lights or encounters.
The trophy pops when you witness one.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by: hit someone with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, swing a bat (or similar melee weapon) from the car window, and knock them over. It is the silliest trophy on the list — one clean hit does it. Use a slow car on a quiet street so you can aim the swing, and expect a wanted level afterwards.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Equip a melee weapon (a bat) and get in a car.
Drive slowly past a pedestrian and swing from the vehicle.
Knock them over — the trophy pops on the hit.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty cash from robberies and heists — you cannot spend them directly, so you wash them through contacts (fences, launderers) for clean money. Rob banks, vaults and trucks to build up Marked Bills, then find your laundering contacts and wash $250,000 in total. The counter is cumulative, so keep laundering as you earn.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Find a laundering contact and wash the bills.
The trophy pops once $250,000 has been laundered in total.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, food, weapons, cars, anything sold in Leonida's stores. The counter is cumulative across every shop type, so it grows naturally as you buy gear for the other trophies. If it is short at the end, buy the most expensive ammo and car upgrades you can find — ammunition is the fastest way to burn cash. Check the stats menu for the running total.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Buy gear, clothes, food and ammo as you play.
Check the stats menu for the cumulative spend.
Top up with expensive ammo or car upgrades to reach $100,000.

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are the property purchases of GTA VI — safehouses with parking, in the series tradition. They appear on the in-game property map as you progress; each costs money, so save up (laundered cash helps). Buy all eight and the trophy pops. Garages also give you somewhere to store the 10 vehicles the Scooter Bros trophy needs.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Save money (launder Marked Bills for clean cash).
Buy garage properties from the in-game property map.
The trophy pops when all 8 are owned.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — Leonida's vehicle-delivery app (the trailers show app-based services all over the city). Open the app, register a vehicle you own or drive (the app likely lets you add a car to its fleet), and repeat for 10 distinct vehicles. Use the cars in your garages — buying all 8 garages gives you plenty to register. The counter is in the app itself.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on the in-game phone.
Register a vehicle to the app.
Repeat for 10 distinct vehicles — the trophy pops on the tenth.
